Quotient Filter: Quotient filters are **mergeable** — build per-partition filters, then combine them with `quotient_filter(q, r, filter)`. Size one explicitly with `q` (holds at most 2^q − 1 values) and `r` (remainder bits per slot, ~2^−r false positive rate), or let `quotient_filter(r, value)` pick `q` for you.
XOR Filters: XOR filters are static — built once, queried many times. ~9 bits per key for the 8-bit variant (0.39% FPR), ~18 bits per key for the 16-bit (0.0015% FPR). ~20% smaller than Bloom for the same false-positive rate.
Binary Fuse Filters: Binary Fuse is the modern best-in-class space-efficient family. <9 bits per key for the 8-bit variant, very fast construction and lookups. Static structure — pick this for read-heavy workloads where storage matters most.
Bloom Filters: Split block Bloom filters — the Parquet Bloom filter format. Sized up front for an expected number of distinct values and a target false positive rate, mergeable with `bloom_filter_merge`, and byte-for-byte the filter DuckDB writes into Parquet files for the same values and sizing.
Inspection: Generic functions that work on any filter BLOB with a bitfilters header — probe it, describe it, or check that it is valid — plus the per-type `*_info` and `*_is_valid` variants.
DuckDB Bloom Filters: Bloom filters in DuckDB's native internal format. Use these when you need to materialize join filters or zone-map-style data-skipping structures that the DuckDB optimizer can consume directly.
